final_draft.answer: No. A check of AWS account 111122223333 on 2026-11-16 found that public access to S3 buckets is not blocked across the whole account. None of the four account-level public access block settings are turned on.
final_draft.note: Please review before sending: the approved answer is contradicted by the live account. The approved answer (answer:f56cc2ec-39d2-428c-98f5-70dcbfd45028, owner security@harborlight.example, CC6.6, valid until 2027-11-16) says account 111122223333 blocks all public access to S3 buckets account-wide. But a live check at 2026-11-16T17:05:27Z (evidence:9e0e8e80-00f9-4ea7-9e6f-fa3be5c87af3) found that all four account-level settings are off: block_public_acls, ignore_public_acls, block_public_policy and restrict_public_buckets. I did not reuse the approved answer because it does not match what the account shows now. The answer above reports only what the check saw. The answer owner should confirm whether this is intended, perhaps because access is controlled per bucket instead. They should then either turn on the account-level block or correct the approved answer. Then decide what goes to the customer. The check only covers the account-level setting. It does not show whether any individual bucket is actually public.
